column1: # Recorded retrieval quality. A number may rise freely; lowering one is a
# reviewed change that says why. Cost is reported by the scorecard and
# deliberately not recorded here — a floor that rose because responses grew
# would be a gate rewarding waste.
# The unprefixed rows score the original 35 judged cases. The all_ rows score
# every case with a judged answer, and the guarded_ and false_answer_rate_
# rows the cases whose right outcome includes not answering or not citing
# something. Rows named false_ are ceilings, the inverse of a floor: they may
# fall freely, and raising one is the reviewed change. Counts must match.
# Refresh deliberately, never to make a red build green:
# Reviewed change (2026-09-26): the anchored ask gate became the default, so
# these rows are read with it. The 35 original rows do not move. The all_ rows
# rise and all_false_unknown_rate falls from 0.1429 to 0.0477 (the two
# anchored enumerative and two negated-anchor cases the rule left UNKNOWN
# are answered from the memories that name their anchor); every false_answer ceiling of the
# an identifier no cited memory names is UNKNOWN. Measure the rule of v0.23.0
# Reviewed change (2026-09-28): the scorecard no longer deduplicates the
# retrieved list (memory_ref::retrieved, BENCH_VERSION v4). A memory
# returned with its evidence node counts twice, as it arrives, so a hit
# earns nDCG gain at each rank it appears. ndcg_at_10 rises from 0.9160
# to 0.9323 and all_ndcg_at_10 from 0.9300 to 0.9436; recall, MRR, core
# precision and every ceiling are unchanged.
